lesson.title: Read a tool call
lesson.subtitle: Split what the model writes into a tool and its details

video.title: Read a tool call
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Joseph Mwangi — computer studies teacher, Kenya (main character)
Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice, talking to the student (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: A list: The model writes only text; Your code reads it; Then things happen.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Here’s a secret about AI agents. The model never touches a tool. It writes a line of text, and your code decides what that text makes happen. Today, you write the code that reads it.

scenes.animation: The Darsi mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: reading a tool call, in Python.

scenes.visual: A list: A plan: what it will do; A call: a tool and its details; An answer for the person.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: When an agent’s model takes a turn, it writes one of three things. A plan: one short sentence about what it will do. A tool call: a tool’s name, then its details. Or an answer for the person.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: weather{"place":"Kafi", …
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Here’s a call that Darsi Tiny really wrote. First comes the tool’s name, weather. Straight after it, the details sit in curly brackets. That part is JSON, a way to write data as text.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: JSON writes data as names and values inside curly brackets. Python reads it with json dot loads, which turns the text into a dictionary. Then args, place, gives you Kafi.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: i = text.find("{") …
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: So how do you split a call? Find the first curly bracket. Everything before it is the tool’s name. Everything from it onwards is the JSON.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Not every text is a call
scenes.narration: But not every text is a call. An answer like Tomorrow in Kafi, sunny, has no curly bracket at all. Then find gives minus one, and your function should return None: there’s no tool to run.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Quick check! You run json dot loads on the details of a call. What do you get back?

scenes.visual: A list: Keys: place, day; It runs nothing; It checks nothing; Your code checks next.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A dictionary. json dot loads only turns text into data: the keys are the details’ names, like place and day. It doesn’t run anything, and it doesn’t check anything. Is Kafi a real village? That’s for your code to check next.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Models make mistakes, so some calls are broken: a missing bracket, a quote in the wrong place. Then json dot loads raises a ValueError, and your agent crashes. Unless you catch it, with try and except.

scenes.visual: A list: Darsi Tiny, on your phone; One step: the plan, then the call; What it sees: plain text.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: inside an agent’s loop
scenes.narration: In the lab, Darsi Tiny runs for real, on your phone. Press One step, and watch it write the plan, then the call. Open What Darsi Tiny sees: the call is plain text, exactly what your function will split.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Your turn. The model wrote: Tomorrow in Kafi, sunny, high thirty-five. What should your function return?

scenes.visual: Summary points: Plan, call or answer; Split at the first {; json.loads gives a dictionary; Catch broken calls.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Plan, call or answer · Split at the first { · json.loads gives a dictionary · Catch broken calls
scenes.narration: None: there’s no curly bracket, so it’s an answer. Remember: the model writes a plan, a call or an answer. Split a call at its first curly bracket, and read the details with json dot loads. Catch broken calls instead of crashing.

scenes.visual: A list: Write five model lines; Swap with a friend; Call, answer or broken?; Name each tool.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it yourself: on paper, write five lines an agent might produce: some calls, some answers, one broken. Swap with a friend. They mark each line as a call, an answer or broken, and name the tool in every call.

checkpoints.prompt: You run json.loads on the details of a call. What do you get back?

options.text: A Python dictionary of the details

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — json.loads turns JSON text into a dictionary: keys like place and day, with their values. It runs nothing.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — json.loads only turns text into data, a dictionary of the details. The tool hasn’t run yet.

checkpoints.prompt: The model wrote “Tomorrow in Kafi: sunny, high 35°C.” What should parse_call return?

options.text: None: it’s an answer, not a call
A ValueError that stops the agent

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — there’s no curly bracket, so find gives -1: it’s an answer to show the person, not a tool to run.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — no curly bracket means it’s an answer. Return None, and show it to the person.
